- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast increase to +3–5% above peak.
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward buffer to forecast.
- When official events are frequent (≥15 events/30d) and bearish sentiment dominates, model overreacts to short-term volatility; smooth 30d forecast with 1–2% downward adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; apply 1–3% downward correction if price is above 75 for 3 consecutive days.
- For 30d forecasts with low sentiment (≤0.33) and low supply net, model tends to underestimate decline; add 1–4% downward adjustment if price is below 70.
- If recent auction supply events are clustered (e.g., 3+ auctions in 5 days), model overestimates price stability; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per event.
